headline: Ahead of Special Town Meeting, Southborough boards split over major funding requests for golf course irrigation and a pedestrian bridge while finalizing warrant recommendations.
synopsis: Ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting, Southborough committees finalized warrant positions on key financial and zoning proposals. Sharp divisions emerged over Community Preservation Act funding requests, with the Advisory Committee recommending against both a $1.087 million golf course irrigation project and a $217,318 supplemental appropriation for the Peninsula Trail footbridge. In contrast, the Advisory Committee unanimously endorsed a $240,000 water main extension to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill and supported establishing a stormwater enterprise fund structure. The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support a zoning amendment easing two-family home conversions, though the Advisory Committee recommended against it due to density and septic concerns. Meanwhile, the Select Board initiated a comprehensive review of the town governance structure, and departments began drafting initial FY28 operating budgets.

top_items.title: Golf course irrigation funding divided town boards
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee unanimously opposed using Community Preservation Act funds for the Southborough Golf Club's $1.087 million irrigation project, while the Golf Committee and Community Preservation Committee backed the article.
top_items.body: Town boards debated Article 3 for the Special Town Meeting, which proposes funding a $1,087,296 irrigation system overhaul at the Southborough Golf Club using $433,546 in new CPA funds, $550,000 in previously authorized CPA funds, and $100,000 from the golf revolving fund. The Advisory Committee voted against the article, arguing capital improvements should be self-funded through golf fees or debt backed by player surcharges rather than taxpayer-funded CPA money. The Golf Committee agreed to move forward with the article as written without seeking floor amendments, approving $500 for informational flyers to present their case directly to voters.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail bridge advanced despite cost objections
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance a $217,318 CPA funding request for a prefabricated footbridge, even as the Select Board and Advisory Committee opposed it over costs.
top_items.body: Article 4 requests $217,318 in additional CPA funding to build a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian bridge along Route 30, bringing total project funding to $428,550. The Advisory Committee and Select Board strongly opposed the measure, citing an estimated cost of approximately $5,000 per linear foot ($320,000 total for the bridge structure). After considering and dropping potential floor amendments to reduce the ask, both the Community Preservation Committee and the Trails Committee decided to present the funding article to Town Meeting as originally printed.

top_items.title: Boards split on two-family dwelling zoning changes
top_items.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to back Article 2 to ease two-family dwelling conversions, while the Advisory Committee issued an unfavorable recommendation citing septic and density concerns.
top_items.body: Article 2 proposes eliminating the two-year ownership requirement for converting single-family houses into two-family dwellings and allowing new two-family construction by special permit. The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to support the warrant article as drafted after evaluating whether the wording could permit two-family homes on undersized business village lots. Conversely, the Advisory Committee recommended against the article, warning it could encourage speculative house flipping, strain septic systems on constrained lots, and increase density in Residential B districts.

top_items.title: Parkerville landfill water main extension recommended
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Article 7, appropriating $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the landfill to municipal water.
top_items.body: Article 7 seeks $240,000 from water retained earnings to extend a municipal water main to two residences near the closed Parkerville Road landfill following contamination testing. Advisory Committee members confirmed with town leadership that the town will cover the installation of service lines extending all the way into the homes, which eliminates potential health risks and avoids ongoing state-mandated private well testing costs.

top_items.title: Select Board reviewed municipal governance study
top_items.why: Consultant Bill Keegan presented initial findings evaluating Southborough's governance model, town manager powers, and board oversight.
top_items.body: Bill Keegan of Capital Strategic Strategies delivered an overview of an 18-week study assessing Southborough's municipal government structure. The study compares Southborough's administration, town manager authority, and structure across its 68 local boards with other Massachusetts towns to evaluate potential shifts between charter and bylaw governance models.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee backed stormwater enterprise accounting framework
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee finalized report language supporting Article 5 to establish a stormwater enterprise fund starting in fiscal year 2028.
top_items.body: Article 5 proposes creating a municipal stormwater enterprise fund as an accounting structure to track stormwater compliance costs and potential revenues. The Advisory Committee clarified in its warrant report that the article does not implement user fees or funding, noting that any future fee system based on impervious surfaces—including charges on tax-exempt parcels—would require separate Town Meeting authorization.

top_items.title: Initial FY28 department operating budgets approved
top_items.why: The Library Trustees and Recreation Commission voted to approve their FY28 operating budget requests as the town prepares for projected structural deficits.
top_items.body: Amid projections of a municipal budget deficit exceeding $2 million for FY28, town departments began approving baseline budget requests. The Library Board of Trustees voted 6-0 to approve its FY28 operating budget, balancing state materials expenditure requirements against rising personnel and network costs, while the Recreation Commission unanimously approved an operating budget request of $4,250.
